claims.evidence: The photo shows an engine assembly, but there are no readable markings or documentation to confirm it is tokumbo (imported used) versus locally sourced.

risks.risk: Wrong engine fitment (vehicle make/model/engine code not identifiable from the photo).
risks.proof: Ask for the engine code/part number (stamped on engine block) and a photo of it, plus the vehicle it came from (make/model/year).
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst case as an unidentified engine with unknown fitment.

risks.risk: Unknown condition (no proof of running, compression, leaks, or missing parts).
risks.proof: Ask for a short video of the engine running (or at least cranking) and photos of key areas: oil pan underside, timing/belt/chain area, and any visible leaks.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst case as not proven working.

risks.risk: Missing accessories/components (the photo may not show everything included).
risks.proof: Ask for a checklist of included parts (starter, alternator, turbo if any, ECU/loom if any) and photos of what is included laid out.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst case as incomplete/unknown inclusions.

risks.risk: Potential damage during removal/transport (cracked housings, bent shafts, broken mounts).
risks.proof: Ask for close-ups of mounting points, any cracks on the block/head, and the oil pump/balance shaft area (if that is what is being sold).
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst case as possibly damaged.

proof_requests: Send a clear photo of the engine code/part number stamped on the engine block (and where it is located).
Send the vehicle details it came from (make/model/year) and confirm compatibility for the buyer’s car.
Send a short video of the engine cranking/running (or proof of working) and show any dashboard/ECU lights if running.
Confirm what exactly is included (starter/alternator/ECU/loom/turbo if applicable) with photos of all accessories laid out.
